name: Chenaniah
overview: Chenaniah was a male Levite who served as a chief among the Levites, specifically noted as a descendant of Izhar, one of the sons of Kohath, who was a son of Levi. This places him within the Izharite clan, a significant family line within the tribe of Levi, entrusted with important religious duties in Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Chenaniah means 'YHWH strengthens,' reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges God's sustaining power. This proper name, recorded in 1 Chronicles 15:22, highlights a common biblical practice of embedding divine attributes within personal names.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Chenaniah as a descendant of Levi, linking him to the priestly lineage through Izhar. Beyond this, there are no further detailed family relationships noted in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Chenaniah's role as a chief of the Levites underscores his leadership within the tribe responsible for worship and temple service. His lineage from Izhar connects him to the Kohathite branch, which held specific duties related to the sanctuary. His mention in 1 Chronicles highlights the organized structure of Levitical service under God's covenant with Israel.
